indicators.text: TLE epoch-to-epoch comparison detects a non-routine in-track, cross-track, or radial maneuver (delta_v >= 1.5 m/s) with calibrated confidence >= 0.75 on a watched non-sibling payload.
indicators.rule: delta_v_ms >= 1.5 and confidence >= 0.75 and not routine_station_keeping
indicators.note: Not live: part of the manoeuvre lane.

indicators.text: Orbit's comparison of two GCAT readings finds a new payload or debris entry from a launch more than 30 days old, possibly from a host object already in orbit.
indicators.rule: new JCAT entry whose launch date is more than 30 days before the reading (gcat.diff, late_groups)
indicators.note: Not diagnostic on its own: breakups and late identifications look the same as releases.

indicators.text: Objects sharing the same international launch designator separate steadily after launch (routine sibling dispersion).
Watched satellite TLE history contains a tracking gap >= 48 hours between consecutive element sets.
indicators.note: Not live: part of the manoeuvre lane.

warning_problems.title: Non-routine orbital maneuver or co-orbital inspection activity
warning_problems.watch_condition: Continuous comparison of consecutive TLE/GP element sets across watched reconnaissance, inspector, and GEO communications/early-warning satellites.
warning_problems.issue_on_change: Issue a warning item when a watched object executes a maneuver with delta_v >= 1.5 m/s and calibrated confidence >= 0.75 outside routine station-keeping.
warning_problems.deactivation: Orbit stabilizes for 14 days with no further delta-v or drift toward another active payload.

hypotheses.title: Deliberate orbital re-phasing, ground-track retargeting, or co-orbital inspection approach
Routine constellation slot maintenance, debris avoidance, or post-launch sibling dispersion
TLE fit noise, solar-storm atmospheric drag spike, or cross-tagging across a tracking gap (artefact)
